requirements.evidence: The whole contract is implemented. Login (app/Livewire/Auth/Login.php:20-51) lowercases the e-mail, uses `email:rfc,strict`, keys the limiter on `Str::transliterate(email|ip)` with 5 attempts, returns `auth.throttle` and `auth.failed` errors on `email`, regenerates the session and calls `redirectIntended(route('home'))`. Register (Register.php:44-75) rate-limits with key 'register|'.ip and 5 attempts, applies the unique/confirmed/`Password::default()` rules, fires Registered, logs in, regenerates and redirects to home. Password::defaults is set once in AppServiceProvider.php:29. Logout (LogoutController.php:15-22) invalidates the session and regenerates the token. Home uses `auth`+`verified` (routes/web.php:36) and redirectUsersTo is set (bootstrap/app.php:17). Forgot password always flashes `passwords.sent` under throttle:6,1. Reset rotates `remember_token` and fires PasswordReset (PasswordResetController.php:51-58). Verification uses EmailVerificationRequest with signed+throttle, and resend skips verified users. .env.example, phpunit.xml pins and both ui.php files are present. Gaps: the task says the no-hardcoded-href rule covers existing views too, but welcome/bulma-test are not in the diff, so their compliance rests only on the new test. Reset and forgot-password do not lowercase the e-mail, while register and login do.

conventions.evidence: Mostly follows the conventions. Login uses `#[Validate]` + `$this->validate()`. There are anonymous Blade components (components/card, field, status) with `@props` and `{{ }}`, Bulma markup, `route()` everywhere, plain `wire:model`, CHANGELOG and docs/business-rules.md updated, and PHPDoc on the public methods. Deviations: Register validates through `rules()` (Register.php:30-37), not the project's `#[Validate]` pattern. PasswordResetController::update validates three fields inline (PasswordResetController.php:43-47), where the conventions call for a Form Request beyond one or two fields. User creation is written directly in the component instead of an Action.

security.evidence: Strong overall. Throttling is per e-mail+IP and per IP, the session is regenerated on login/register and invalidated on logout, and the password reset gives no enumeration signal (the broker status is ignored and `passwords.sent` is always flashed). remember_token is rotated. EmailVerificationRequest returns 403 for a tampered id. Mass assignment goes through `#[Fillable]`, and the password field never echoes its value (field.blade.php:12). There are no secrets in public properties. Limited weakness: layouts/app.blade.php:13 loads Bulma from a third-party CDN without Subresource Integrity when no Vite build exists.

tests.evidence: Broad feature coverage across 6 files: pt_BR/en rendering, guest/auth redirects, throttling (login, register, forgot 429, verify, resend), the tampered verification id (EmailVerificationTest.php:55-63), the reset token/rule/confirmation, remember_token rotation, the single name="email" input, and the no-hardcoded-links scan. Weak spots: 'remember me sets the recaller cookie' (LoginTest.php:74-85) is vacuous, because `Auth::getRecallerName()` is never null and the factory already sets remember_token. 'login ignores tampered locked state' (LoginTest.php:164-172) is a plain wrong-credentials test, not a tamper test. No test covers an authenticated user calling the Livewire `submit` actions directly, which is the unauthorized-call case the Livewire policy requires.

simplicity.evidence: The change is lean. It uses framework primitives (Password broker, EmailVerificationRequest, redirectUsersTo, RateLimiter) and three small reusable Blade components with no extra layers. The only speculative addition is the CDN fallback branch in layouts/app.blade.php:12-14.

readability.evidence: Names are clear and methods small, with focused controllers and constants for MAX_ATTEMPTS. Minor issues: the misleading test name at LoginTest.php:164, and docs/business-rules.md:139 adds a `## Authentication` heading with no blank line before it.

scope.evidence: Almost everything serves the task, including the pt_BR validation attribute names (lang/pt_BR/validation.php:198-203). The unrequested CDN stylesheet fallback (layouts/app.blade.php:12-14) is mildly out of scope next to the 'no SCSS/JS changes' boundary.

issues.explanation: The test named as a tamper test only submits wrong credentials, and no test checks that an authenticated user calling the guest-only Livewire `submit` actions is refused, so the Livewire policy's unauthorized-call/tamper requirement is not really covered.
The 'remember me' test is vacuous: `Auth::getRecallerName()` always returns a name and the factory already sets a remember_token, so it passes even if `$remember` is ignored.
Register validates with a `rules()` method, while the project's documented Livewire pattern is `#[Validate]` attributes (which Login follows).
The reset request validates three fields inline, while the conventions require a Form Request once rules go beyond one or two fields.
The fallback loads Bulma from jsDelivr without an integrity/crossorigin attribute, which adds an unpinned third-party asset that the task did not ask for.
Forgot and reset password do not lowercase the e-mail, unlike login and register, so a mixed-case input may not find the lowercase-stored user on a case-sensitive database.
The task says the route()-only rule applies to existing views too, but those views are not in the diff, so their compliance is not shown beyond the new scanning test.
User creation is written directly in the component instead of an `app/Actions/*` class, while the conventions route domain writes through Actions.
The new `## Authentication` heading follows the previous list item with no blank line before it.

review.summary: The change builds the full session-auth flow (Livewire login/register, logout, forgot/reset password, e-mail verification, verified /home) with Bulma Blade components, pt_BR-first translations, the locale pins, throttling and session hardening, plus extensive Pest feature tests and doc updates. It meets the contract and is secure. The remaining issues are small: Register uses `rules()` instead of `#[Validate]`, the reset request has no Form Request, a couple of weak or misnamed Livewire tests leave the unauthorized-call/tamper cases uncovered, and there is an unrequested CDN fallback. I would approve it with nits.
